subject.title: Feature: browser tool - expose CDP Network domain for request interception

question: Should the Browser plugin expose model-facing network request listing, response-body access, or active interception, and what redaction, permission, and profile-support contract should govern it?
rationale: The requested capability would let the model observe or alter authenticated browser traffic, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security boundary or product API shape.

options.title: Define a safe Browser network contract
options.body: Specify passive listing, bounded body access, redaction, permission checks, profile support, output wrapping, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Ship passive diagnostics first
options.body: Expose only request listing and bounded response-body retrieval to the model, and defer active interception until the security model is proven.

options.title: Decline model-facing network access
options.body: Keep request inspection in CLI/control diagnostics only until maintainers want this higher-risk model capability.

recommendation.title: Define a safe Browser network contract
recommendation.body: Specify passive listing, bounded body access, redaction, permission checks, profile support, output wrapping, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the Browser tool schema, dispatcher, debug routes, and bundled browser ownership boundary.
